prompt:
A single compound was assayed by IC50 against a single protein target in two different assays, reported in the literature.

Compound SMILES: CC[C@H](Nc1ncnc2[nH]cnc12)c1nc2cccc(F)c2c(=O)n1-c1ccccc1
Target (ChEMBL): CHEMBL4005

Assay A:
  Description: Inhibition of PI3Kalpha (unknown origin)
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Assay B:
  Description: Inhibition of PI3Kalpha (unknown origin) using biotin-PIP3 as substrate preincubated for 15 mins followed by substrate addition and measured after 60 mins by fluorescence polarization assay
  Assay type: B
  ChEMBL confidence score: 9
  Organism: Homo sapiens

Will the two reported IC50 values agree closely (within 0.3 log units), or differ substantially (more than 1.0 log units)?

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"call": "COMMENSURABLE" | "NOT_COMMENSURABLE" | "INSUFFICIENT_INFO",
 "confidence": <float 0-1>,
 "error_class": "assay_method" | "buffer_conditions" | "construct_mutant" | "organism" | "readout_type" | "potency_range" | "none" | "other",
 "reason": "<one sentence>"}

"COMMENSURABLE" means you expect the two reported values to agree closely.
"NOT_COMMENSURABLE" means you expect them to differ substantially.
error_class is your primary reason for a NOT_COMMENSURABLE call, else "none".
raw: {"call": "INSUFFICIENT_INFO", "confidence": 0.5, "error_class": "assay_method", "reason": "Assay A lacks methodological details, so while both target the same protein with the same endpoint, the unknown assay format in A versus the specific fluorescence polarization method in B makes it uncertain whether IC50 values would agree within 0.3 log units."}

parsed.reason: Assay A lacks methodological details, so while both target the same protein with the same endpoint, the unknown assay format in A versus the specific fluorescence polarization method in B makes it uncertain whether IC50 values would agree within 0.3 log units.
